topic: Effectiveness of Dance-Based Interventions on Depression for Persons With MCI and Dementia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

sources.title: Effectiveness of Dance-Based Interventions on Depression for Persons With MCI and Dementia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.authors: Wang Y, Liu M, Tan Y, Dong Z, Wu J, Cui H, Shen D, Chi I.

findings.finding: Dance-based interventions significantly decrease depression compared to control groups.
findings.quote: There were significant differences in decreasing depression in favor of dance-based interventions compared with controls [SMD = -0.42, 95% CI (-0.60, -0.23), p < 0.00001].

findings.finding: Effects diminish during follow-up data post-intervention.
findings.quote: Compared with the post-intervention data, the follow-up data indicated diminishing effects (Cohen's d = 0.1355).

findings.finding: Dance-based interventions show varying effectiveness depending on the condition and frequency.
findings.quote: Dance-based interventions were more effective in reducing depression for persons with dementia than with those having MCI, and were more effective with the delivery frequency of 1 h twice a week than 35 min 2-3 times a week.

principle: Dance-based interventions effectively alleviate depression in persons with mild cognitive impairment and dementia, with greater effectiveness observed in dementia compared to MCI.
for_the_teacher: Design lessons that run for one hour, scheduled twice a week for optimal mood benefits.
Provide regular, ongoing dance sessions to help prevent the diminishing of positive emotional effects over time.
when_it_does_not_apply: One included study showed no significant benefit on anxiety rating scores.
